features.name: Typographical accuracy
features.description: This captures how free of spelling and mechanical errors the letter is and how polished it feels as a result.

levels.descriptor: Frequent obvious errors throughout the letter noticeably undermine professionalism.
Several clear errors appear, but the letter remains understandable.
Only a few minor errors appear.
The letter is essentially error-free and polished.

features.evidence: the chance to build systems whose success is measured in incidents that never occur
features.name: Role motivation clarity
features.description: This captures how clearly the letter explains why this specific security engineering role is a compelling next step for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in applying with little reason for this role in particular.
States interest in the role but with broad or familiar reasoning.
Gives a clear role-specific reason tied to security engineering, automation, or impact.
Articulates a distinctive and memorable rationale that tightly links prior experience to this exact mandate.

features.evidence: foundational infrastructure is where I choose to work
features.name: Foundational tooling orientation
features.description: This captures whether the applicant frames their preferred impact as building central infrastructure or shared tooling used by many teams.

levels.descriptor: Does not signal interest in platform or shared-tooling work.
Hints at broad impact but does not make foundational work a clear preference.
Clearly says they prefer central systems or shared tooling.
Makes high-leverage platform work a core part of their professional identity and motivation.

features.evidence: helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default
features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter presents security as something that should help developers through better defaults, lower friction, or proactive support.

levels.descriptor: Does not address developer experience or frames security mainly as control.
Shows general willingness to work with developers.
Explicitly emphasizes reducing friction or making secure behavior easier for developers.
Makes developer enablement a central security philosophy and ties examples to that philosophy.

features.name: Relevant experience duration
features.description: This captures how much professional software development time the letter claims for work relevant to the role.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of relevant experience is stated or experience is unclear.
2 to 3 years of relevant experience is stated.
4 to 5 years of relevant experience is stated.
6 or more years of relevant experience is stated.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: This captures how much shipped production responsibility the applicant claims through the number of services they tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: No concrete production ownership is described.
Claims ownership of 1 to 2 production services or similarly limited scope.
Claims ownership of 3 to 4 production services or repeated production delivery.
Claims ownership of 5 or more production services or broad repeated delivery responsibility.

features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: This captures the level of formal academic training the applicant presents.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree is mentioned or the educational background is unclear.
Presents a Bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Presents a Master's degree.
Presents a Doctoral degree.

features.evidence: Go is my principal programming language
features.name: Go centrality
features.description: This captures how central Go appears to the applicant's recent production work rather than being just one language among many.

levels.descriptor: Does not provide meaningful evidence of Go use.
Mentions some Go exposure but not as a core language.
Presents Go as a major working language in production.
Presents Go as the principal or dominant language across core services.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: This captures the range of additional programming languages the applicant claims beyond Go.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: This captures how substantial the applicant's Python work sounds, especially for production services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Mentions Python briefly or only as light scripting.
Describes regular Python use for tooling, automation, or services.
Shows deep Python ownership across production services or critical internal tooling.

features.evidence: evaluation scaffolding required to deploy them responsibly
features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has hands-on AI experience and whether they frame it in terms of reliable production deployment rather than novelty.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.evidence: Python agents handle repetitive analysis while Go services define their permissions
features.name: Agent architecture ownership
features.description: This captures how concretely the letter claims design responsibility for agentic systems that combine Python agents with Go infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic work is mentioned.
Mentions agents in passing without clear ownership.
Describes building agentic tools or pipelines end to end.
Describes explicit architectural choices such as permissions, boundaries, auditability, or supervision.

features.name: Security assessment rigor
features.description: This captures the depth and concreteness of the applicant's claimed experience performing security assessments.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Claims general security review experience without method detail.
Gives concrete assessment activities such as threat modeling, code review, or attack-surface analysis.
Describes structured assessment practice that includes documentation, remediation verification, or broad stack coverage.

features.name: Vulnerability automation ownership
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has built tooling to reduce manual vulnerability handling and how substantial that ownership was.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability handling automation is mentioned.
Mentions vulnerability work without claiming tool ownership.
Describes building automation for intake, triage, classification, or routing.
Describes end-to-end automation ownership with clear operational effect such as deduplication, prioritization, or major manual workload reduction.

features.evidence: reworked a matching algorithm whose naive form had quietly become a bottleneck
features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: This captures how convincingly the letter demonstrates practical use of data structures or algorithms to improve real systems.

levels.descriptor: Provides no evidence of data structure or algorithm work.
Claims strength abstractly without a concrete example.
Gives one concrete example of algorithmic improvement.
Gives a concrete example that clearly changed performance, tractability, or system design.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: This captures the level of formal security credentialing the applicant chooses to present.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Presents a foundational credential such as Security+ or similar baseline training.
Presents a strong hands-on credential such as OSCP.
Presents multiple relevant credentials or unusually strong formal security credentialing.

features.name: Offensive practice intensity
features.description: This captures how actively the applicant maintains an attacker's perspective through capture-the-flag competition or similar practice.

levels.descriptor: No offensive practice is mentioned.
Mentions occasional participation without depth or results.
Describes regular participation or serious engagement.
Reports strong placements or sustained high-level competition.

features.evidence: write the patch and send it upstream
features.name: Open source stewardship
features.description: This captures whether the applicant shows responsibility beyond their employer by contributing to or maintaining open-source software.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Makes a vague contribution claim without concrete ownership.
Describes submitting patches or fixes upstream.
Describes maintaining or releasing an open-source project with outside users or contributors.

features.name: Personal build ambition
features.description: This captures how technically ambitious the applicant's self-directed projects appear outside their day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions only a small utility or simple app used mainly as a curiosity exercise.
Describes a solid standalone project with nontrivial engineering scope.
Describes a substantial systems project involving demanding concerns such as distribution, failover, consensus, or recovery.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned to the team
features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: This captures how much the letter supports claims with concrete examples, ownership, or outcomes rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists qualities or interests with little supporting evidence.
Includes a few examples but limited detail on ownership or effect.
Gives concrete examples of work with enough detail to make the claims credible.
Repeatedly ties claims to specific actions and clear outcomes or impact.
